items.why: Falling from above the frame, A lands on the pillar top, the only surface under the fall.
From the crouch on the pillar top A tips over the edge and runs down the pillar face toward B.
Running down the pillar face, A kicks off it with both feet to arc toward B.
The kick-off leaves A descending toward B with no footing, so B throws the kunai up at A mid-descent.
B's kunai flies up at A, so A meets it with the right sole and stamps it back down to the ground.
The deflect drops A onto both feet, squared up to B, the rope dart in the left hand.
A lands inside B's reach, so B charges with a rising palm at A's chest.
B's rising palm is about to hit A's chest, so A escapes by substitution: a smoke burst, and the log takes A's place.
The log now stands where A was, so B's palm hits the log, not A, and B is thrown off balance.
B is off balance against the log, so A reappears behind B, unseen.
Behind B, with B's back exposed, A drives the right knee into B's spine.
The knee launches B forward into the air, and A follows with an aerial backflip kick.
Kicked away, B recovers mid-air and answers with exactly three shuriken at A.
Three shuriken fly at A, so A slides under them; they pass over A into the pillar.
The slide carries A under B's guard, and A rises out of it into a cartwheel, left elbow driving up at B's chest.
A's rising elbow comes at B, so B catches the left elbow and throws A toward the pillar.
Thrown at the pillar, A meets it with the feet, pushes off and lands crouched by the rope dart.
Crouched by the rope dart with it in the left hand, A whips it out to wrap B's right shoulder.
With the rope dart wrapped on B's shoulder, A pulls the line taut and drags B toward the pillar, into A's reach.
B is dragged into reach on the taut line, so A drives the kunai into B's right shoulder.
The kunai drive carries B down, and A and B crash to the ground together.
Slammed down with the kunai in the shoulder, B stays down, and A holds the crouch over B.

[SCENE]
10s anime fight, 24fps, moonlit bamboo courtyard, tall wooden pillar at back z=6 extending from ground y=0 to y=8, dark under-canopy of bamboo on left. A: lean ninja, dark coat, red scarf wrapped SMALL at neck, face fully visible. B: broad ninja, grey armor, one shoulder pauldron. TWO fighters, FIVE props (kunai, rope dart, smoke pellet, shuriken volley, substitution log). A starts ABOVE the frame, falling from y=10. B starts at z=4.5 facing -Z. Naruto-tier choreography with substitution and teleport-position counters. Euler degrees XYZ. Render spec exactly.
10 s anime scene, 24 fps, setting: moonlit bamboo courtyard.
Cast: A = lean ninja: Lean figure in a dark coat; red scarf wrapped small at the neck; face fully visible; Dark coat, red scarf wrapped SMALL at the neck, face fully visible. B = broad ninja: Broad figure in grey armor with one shoulder pauldron; Grey armor, one shoulder pauldron.
Props at the start: kunai (made of steel, held by B R hand, embedded loose until 8.50); rope dart (made of steel and hemp, carried by A, line coiled until 8.00); smoke pellet (made of clay and powder, carried by A, smoke sealed until 3.70); shuriken volley (3 shuriken, made of steel, carried by B, flight holstered until 5.10); substitution log (made of wood, on the ground, deployment standing until 3.70).
Render intent. Motion: fast, strong, heavy, sudden accelerations into the accents; readable at one shot every 0.5 s on average. Animation: anime; spacing: 36 dense, 2 medium and 2 sparse gaps between lines; 7 smears on declared limbs or props, 6 impact frames. Choreography: every effect follows its cause along the causal links; final instruction: end on A hold crouch over b, B remains down.

[MOVEMENT LANGUAGE]
Labanotation written as words. Mode: Mixed: staff lines primary; Root [x, y, z] + EulerXYZ [x, y, z] on strike lines and on each performer's first and last line, as precision override.
Each line = one measure for one performer; time in seconds; a symbol lasts until the next line.
SUPPORT names what bears the weight; NO SUPPORT = airborne.
Contact bow = touch; [contact: X-Y retained] = held; [contact: Y ENDS – released] = let go; DOUBLE BOW + accent = a strike (interp.: a momentary contact with a strong accent).
Directions are relative to the performer's front: forward, back, left, right and the diagonals between them; levels high, mid, low; place-high / place-low = straight up / down. A limb reads mid while within 45 degrees of horizontal (interp.). Lower arm and lower leg: straight, or folded by degrees.
Turns name the axis and the plane: a flip turns about the side-to-side axis (sagittal plane), a spin about the vertical axis (transverse plane), a cartwheel about the front-to-back axis (frontal plane); each turn is written once, on the line where it starts, with its count.
Precision tags: [f:L|R|both] feet, [h:L|R|both] hands, [f:alt] stepping, _on_<surface> when the support is not the ground.
Explicit = the written lines (every support change, contact and accent has one); implied = everything between lines.
position: [x, y, z] is the performer's root in scene metres, on every line that has no Root block.
Root [x, y, z] is the scene position in metres; EulerXYZ and joints are degrees.
A word in capitals before a bow or contact (CATCH, DEFLECT, STRIKE, THROW) names the combat action it performs; the Effort below stays Laban.

[CAUSAL LINKS]
→ hard cause (the effect starts after the cause ends); ⇢ soft cause (it may start while the cause runs).
A fall from above ⇢ A land pillar top ⇢ A sprint down pillar ⇢ A kick off pillar ⇢ B throw kunai → A foot deflect kunai ⇢ A land facing opponent ⇢ B rising palm charge ⇢ A kawarimi substitution → B palm hits log ⇢ A reappear behind opponent ⇢ A knee strike spine ⇢ A aerial backflip kick ⇢ B throw shuriken volley ⇢ A slide under volley ⇢ A cartwheel rising elbow ⇢ B catch elbow throw ⇢ A wall push off pillar → A rope dart regrapple ⇢ A pull toward pillar ⇢ A aerial kunai drive ⇢ A crash to ground ⇢ A hold crouch over opponent
Why each link holds:
A fall from above ⇢ A land pillar top: Falling from above the frame, A lands on the pillar top, the only surface under the fall.
A land pillar top ⇢ A sprint down pillar: From the crouch on the pillar top A tips over the edge and runs down the pillar face toward B.
A sprint down pillar ⇢ A kick off pillar: Running down the pillar face, A kicks off it with both feet to arc toward B.
A kick off pillar ⇢ B throw kunai: The kick-off leaves A descending toward B with no footing, so B throws the kunai up at A mid-descent.
B throw kunai → A foot deflect kunai: B's kunai flies up at A, so A meets it with the right sole and stamps it back down to the ground.
A foot deflect kunai ⇢ A land facing opponent: The deflect drops A onto both feet, squared up to B, the rope dart in the left hand.
A land facing opponent ⇢ B rising palm charge: A lands inside B's reach, so B charges with a rising palm at A's chest.
B rising palm charge ⇢ A kawarimi substitution: B's rising palm is about to hit A's chest, so A escapes by substitution: a smoke burst, and the log takes A's place.
A kawarimi substitution → B palm hits log: The log now stands where A was, so B's palm hits the log, not A, and B is thrown off balance.
B palm hits log ⇢ A reappear behind opponent: B is off balance against the log, so A reappears behind B, unseen.
A reappear behind opponent ⇢ A knee strike spine: Behind B, with B's back exposed, A drives the right knee into B's spine.
A knee strike spine ⇢ A aerial backflip kick: The knee launches B forward into the air, and A follows with an aerial backflip kick.
A aerial backflip kick ⇢ B throw shuriken volley: Kicked away, B recovers mid-air and answers with exactly three shuriken at A.
B throw shuriken volley ⇢ A slide under volley: Three shuriken fly at A, so A slides under them; they pass over A into the pillar.
A slide under volley ⇢ A cartwheel rising elbow: The slide carries A under B's guard, and A rises out of it into a cartwheel, left elbow driving up at B's chest.
A cartwheel rising elbow ⇢ B catch elbow throw: A's rising elbow comes at B, so B catches the left elbow and throws A toward the pillar.
B catch elbow throw ⇢ A wall push off pillar: Thrown at the pillar, A meets it with the feet, pushes off and lands crouched by the rope dart.
A wall push off pillar → A rope dart regrapple: Crouched by the rope dart with it in the left hand, A whips it out to wrap B's right shoulder.
A rope dart regrapple ⇢ A pull toward pillar: With the rope dart wrapped on B's shoulder, A pulls the line taut and drags B toward the pillar, into A's reach.
A pull toward pillar ⇢ A aerial kunai drive: B is dragged into reach on the taut line, so A drives the kunai into B's right shoulder.
A aerial kunai drive ⇢ A crash to ground: The kunai drive carries B down, and A and B crash to the ground together.
A crash to ground ⇢ A hold crouch over opponent: Slammed down with the kunai in the shoulder, B stays down, and A holds the crouch over B.

- Laban support and contacts are primary; Euler numbers are precision override only.

- TWO fighter identities A and B never merge or duplicate

- Anything embedded in the pillar or a body stays there for the rest of the scene.
- A substitution leaves the substitution log where the body was; the body reappears somewhere else.
- A thrown weapon leaves the hand and does not return without a declared catch.
- The smoke cloud stays where the pellet burst; it does not follow anyone.
- substitution log is a WOODEN BLOCK NOT a fighter
- Identity is immutable: every performer and prop stays itself for the whole scene.
- Spatial continuity: a body travels through space between lines, never faster than 25 m/s; only a declared substitution may jump (the decoy is revealed and the body reappears at its next line).
- Momentum is conserved: a body keeps moving the way the last force sent it until something stops it.
- Ground force needs support: pushing, bracing and striking from the ground need a supporting part.
- Contact before effect: nothing reacts to a hit before the contact.
- Rotation is continuous: turns, flips and cartwheels sweep through every angle in between.

A: lean ninja, dark coat, red scarf wrapped SMALL at neck, face fully visible. B: broad ninja, grey armor, one shoulder pauldron. 10 s anime scene, 24 fps, setting: moonlit bamboo courtyard.
Cast: A = lean ninja: Lean figure in a dark coat; red scarf wrapped small at the neck; face fully visible; Dark coat, red scarf wrapped SMALL at the neck, face fully visible. B = broad ninja: Broad figure in grey armor with one shoulder pauldron; Grey armor, one shoulder pauldron.
Props at the start: kunai (made of steel, held by B R hand, embedded loose until 8.50); rope dart (made of steel and hemp, carried by A, line coiled until 8.00); smoke pellet (made of clay and powder, carried by A, smoke sealed until 3.70); shuriken volley (3 shuriken, made of steel, carried by B, flight holstered until 5.10); substitution log (made of wood, on the ground, deployment standing until 3.70).
Render intent. Motion: fast, strong, heavy, sudden accelerations into the accents; readable at one shot every 0.5 s on average. Animation: anime; spacing: 36 dense, 2 medium and 2 sparse gaps between lines; 7 smears on declared limbs or props, 6 impact frames. Choreography: every effect follows its cause along the causal links; final instruction: end on A hold crouch over b, B remains down.

[MOVEMENT LANGUAGE]
Labanotation written as words. Mode: pure staff: the staff words carry the movement; the only numbers are each line's position.
Each line = one measure for one performer; time in seconds; a symbol lasts until the next line.
SUPPORT names what bears the weight; NO SUPPORT = airborne.
Contact bow = touch; [contact: X-Y retained] = held; [contact: Y ENDS – released] = let go; DOUBLE BOW + accent = a strike (interp.: a momentary contact with a strong accent).
Directions are relative to the performer's front: forward, back, left, right and the diagonals between them; levels high, mid, low; place-high / place-low = straight up / down. A limb reads mid while within 45 degrees of horizontal (interp.). Lower arm and lower leg: straight, or folded by degrees.
Turns name the axis and the plane: a flip turns about the side-to-side axis (sagittal plane), a spin about the vertical axis (transverse plane), a cartwheel about the front-to-back axis (frontal plane); each turn is written once, on the line where it starts, with its count.
Precision tags: [f:L|R|both] feet, [h:L|R|both] hands, [f:alt] stepping, _on_<surface> when the support is not the ground.
Explicit = the written lines (every support change, contact and accent has one); implied = everything between lines.
position: [x, y, z] is the performer's root in scene metres, on every line that has no Root block.
A word in capitals before a bow or contact (CATCH, DEFLECT, STRIKE, THROW) names the combat action it performs; the Effort below stays Laban.

[CAUSAL LINKS]
→ hard cause (the effect starts after the cause ends); ⇢ soft cause (it may start while the cause runs).
A fall from above ⇢ A land pillar top ⇢ A sprint down pillar ⇢ A kick off pillar ⇢ B throw kunai → A foot deflect kunai ⇢ A land facing opponent ⇢ B rising palm charge ⇢ A kawarimi substitution → B palm hits log ⇢ A reappear behind opponent ⇢ A knee strike spine ⇢ A aerial backflip kick ⇢ B throw shuriken volley ⇢ A slide under volley ⇢ A cartwheel rising elbow ⇢ B catch elbow throw ⇢ A wall push off pillar → A rope dart regrapple ⇢ A pull toward pillar ⇢ A aerial kunai drive ⇢ A crash to ground ⇢ A hold crouch over opponent
Why each link holds:
A fall from above ⇢ A land pillar top: Falling from above the frame, A lands on the pillar top, the only surface under the fall.
A land pillar top ⇢ A sprint down pillar: From the crouch on the pillar top A tips over the edge and runs down the pillar face toward B.
A sprint down pillar ⇢ A kick off pillar: Running down the pillar face, A kicks off it with both feet to arc toward B.
A kick off pillar ⇢ B throw kunai: The kick-off leaves A descending toward B with no footing, so B throws the kunai up at A mid-descent.
B throw kunai → A foot deflect kunai: B's kunai flies up at A, so A meets it with the right sole and stamps it back down to the ground.
A foot deflect kunai ⇢ A land facing opponent: The deflect drops A onto both feet, squared up to B, the rope dart in the left hand.
A land facing opponent ⇢ B rising palm charge: A lands inside B's reach, so B charges with a rising palm at A's chest.
B rising palm charge ⇢ A kawarimi substitution: B's rising palm is about to hit A's chest, so A escapes by substitution: a smoke burst, and the log takes A's place.
A kawarimi substitution → B palm hits log: The log now stands where A was, so B's palm hits the log, not A, and B is thrown off balance.
B palm hits log ⇢ A reappear behind opponent: B is off balance against the log, so A reappears behind B, unseen.
A reappear behind opponent ⇢ A knee strike spine: Behind B, with B's back exposed, A drives the right knee into B's spine.
A knee strike spine ⇢ A aerial backflip kick: The knee launches B forward into the air, and A follows with an aerial backflip kick.
A aerial backflip kick ⇢ B throw shuriken volley: Kicked away, B recovers mid-air and answers with exactly three shuriken at A.
B throw shuriken volley ⇢ A slide under volley: Three shuriken fly at A, so A slides under them; they pass over A into the pillar.
A slide under volley ⇢ A cartwheel rising elbow: The slide carries A under B's guard, and A rises out of it into a cartwheel, left elbow driving up at B's chest.
A cartwheel rising elbow ⇢ B catch elbow throw: A's rising elbow comes at B, so B catches the left elbow and throws A toward the pillar.
B catch elbow throw ⇢ A wall push off pillar: Thrown at the pillar, A meets it with the feet, pushes off and lands crouched by the rope dart.
A wall push off pillar → A rope dart regrapple: Crouched by the rope dart with it in the left hand, A whips it out to wrap B's right shoulder.
A rope dart regrapple ⇢ A pull toward pillar: With the rope dart wrapped on B's shoulder, A pulls the line taut and drags B toward the pillar, into A's reach.
A pull toward pillar ⇢ A aerial kunai drive: B is dragged into reach on the taut line, so A drives the kunai into B's right shoulder.
A aerial kunai drive ⇢ A crash to ground: The kunai drive carries B down, and A and B crash to the ground together.
A crash to ground ⇢ A hold crouch over opponent: Slammed down with the kunai in the shoulder, B stays down, and A holds the crouch over B.

[CAUSAL LINKS]
→ hard cause (the effect starts after the cause ends); ⇢ soft cause (it may start while the cause runs).
A fall from above ⇢ A land pillar top ⇢ A sprint down pillar ⇢ A kick off pillar ⇢ B throw kunai → A foot deflect kunai ⇢ A land facing opponent ⇢ B rising palm charge ⇢ A kawarimi substitution → B palm hits log ⇢ A reappear behind opponent ⇢ A knee strike spine ⇢ A aerial backflip kick ⇢ B throw shuriken volley ⇢ A slide under volley ⇢ A cartwheel rising elbow ⇢ B catch elbow throw ⇢ A wall push off pillar → A rope dart regrapple ⇢ A pull toward pillar ⇢ A aerial kunai drive ⇢ A crash to ground ⇢ A hold crouch over opponent
Why each link holds:
A fall from above ⇢ A land pillar top: Falling from above the frame, A lands on the pillar top, the only surface under the fall.
A land pillar top ⇢ A sprint down pillar: From the crouch on the pillar top A tips over the edge and runs down the pillar face toward B.
A sprint down pillar ⇢ A kick off pillar: Running down the pillar face, A kicks off it with both feet to arc toward B.
A kick off pillar ⇢ B throw kunai: The kick-off leaves A descending toward B with no footing, so B throws the kunai up at A mid-descent.
B throw kunai → A foot deflect kunai: B's kunai flies up at A, so A meets it with the right sole and stamps it back down to the ground.
A foot deflect kunai ⇢ A land facing opponent: The deflect drops A onto both feet, squared up to B, the rope dart in the left hand.
A land facing opponent ⇢ B rising palm charge: A lands inside B's reach, so B charges with a rising palm at A's chest.
B rising palm charge ⇢ A kawarimi substitution: B's rising palm is about to hit A's chest, so A escapes by substitution: a smoke burst, and the log takes A's place.
A kawarimi substitution → B palm hits log: The log now stands where A was, so B's palm hits the log, not A, and B is thrown off balance.
B palm hits log ⇢ A reappear behind opponent: B is off balance against the log, so A reappears behind B, unseen.
A reappear behind opponent ⇢ A knee strike spine: Behind B, with B's back exposed, A drives the right knee into B's spine.
A knee strike spine ⇢ A aerial backflip kick: The knee launches B forward into the air, and A follows with an aerial backflip kick.
A aerial backflip kick ⇢ B throw shuriken volley: Kicked away, B recovers mid-air and answers with exactly three shuriken at A.
B throw shuriken volley ⇢ A slide under volley: Three shuriken fly at A, so A slides under them; they pass over A into the pillar.
A slide under volley ⇢ A cartwheel rising elbow: The slide carries A under B's guard, and A rises out of it into a cartwheel, left elbow driving up at B's chest.
A cartwheel rising elbow ⇢ B catch elbow throw: A's rising elbow comes at B, so B catches the left elbow and throws A toward the pillar.
B catch elbow throw ⇢ A wall push off pillar: Thrown at the pillar, A meets it with the feet, pushes off and lands crouched by the rope dart.
A wall push off pillar → A rope dart regrapple: Crouched by the rope dart with it in the left hand, A whips it out to wrap B's right shoulder.
A rope dart regrapple ⇢ A pull toward pillar: With the rope dart wrapped on B's shoulder, A pulls the line taut and drags B toward the pillar, into A's reach.
A pull toward pillar ⇢ A aerial kunai drive: B is dragged into reach on the taut line, so A drives the kunai into B's right shoulder.
A aerial kunai drive ⇢ A crash to ground: The kunai drive carries B down, and A and B crash to the ground together.
A crash to ground ⇢ A hold crouch over opponent: Slammed down with the kunai in the shoulder, B stays down, and A holds the crouch over B.
